title: Add Token Authentication and Permissions
description: Secure the API so that only authenticated users can create, update, or delete posts.
problemStatement:
## Your Mission

Extend the `PostViewSet` from Task 2 to enforce the following:
- Any user (authenticated or not) can list posts (GET `/posts/`) and view a single post (GET `/posts/{id}/`).
- Only authenticated users can create, update, or delete posts.

Use token authentication. Add the `rest_framework.authtoken` app, run migrations, and create a token for a user. Test the API by sending requests with the `Authorization: Token <key>` header.

Also, automatically set the `author` of a new post to the currently authenticated user (override `perform_create`).
hints: Set `authentication_classes` in the viewset to `[TokenAuthentication]` or globally in settings.
expectedOutput: Unauthenticated requests can only GET; POST/PUT/DELETE return 403 Forbidden. Authenticated requests with a valid token can perform all actions.
solutionCode:
# views.py
from rest_framework import viewsets, permissions
from rest_framework.authentication import TokenAuthentication
from .models import Post
from .serializers import PostSerializer

class PostViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    queryset = Post.objects.all()
    serializer_class = PostSerializer
    authentication_classes = [TokenAuthentication]
    permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly]

    def perform_create(self, serializer):
        serializer.save(author=self.request.user)

# settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    ...
    'rest_framework.authtoken',
]

REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    'DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES': [
        'rest_framework.authentication.TokenAuthentication',
    ],
}

# After adding authtoken, run migrate, then create a token for a user in the shell:
# from rest_framework.authtoken.models import Token; token = Token.objects.create(user=user)
